answer: Anchor each agent identity to a small kernel of verifiable history: before an identity can trade, it must accumulate attestations from distinct, already-trusted peers over time, and post a bond that is slashed on fraud. A Sybil attacker starting from the nadir — no history, no endorsements — must therefore buy or forge that history separately for every fake, while honest agents let one identity wander across tasks and build reputation once. Fakes stay cheap to create but expensive to make credible, so flooding the market costs more than the influence it buys.
